Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can size the PoC and alignment test properly.

Summary (high level)
- Orpheus target envelope: p95 end-to-end <= 120ms, p99 end-to-end <= 350ms for the user-facing generation calls we discussed.
- Traffic profile: baseline ~200 qps with short bursts up to ~1k qps for bulk uploads; mix of synchronous text generation (80%) and streaming (20%).
- Key constraints: KV/prefix cache allowed; TLS and mutual auth required; no PHI in test dataset.

Immediate asks (can you confirm):
1) Is the p95/p99 envelope above representative of what you're measuring today with your incumbent? If not, please paste the typical numbers.
2) Can you confirm the streaming-to-sync ratio (we heard ~20% streaming during peak) and whether your client uses long-held streams (>=10s) or many short streams (<2s)?
3) Any procurement/security contacts we should loop in before we share the PoC runbook?

Next steps we propose:
- Engineering-run PoC window (2 business days): controlled traffic replay + live canary (5% of traffic) to compare Redwood hosted vs current provider.
- We'll provide a traffic_profile.csv and a checklist (attached) with exact request shapes, sequence lengths, and expected token counts. Ben will outline the acceptance probe steps.

If you confirm the envelope above, we can schedule the kickoff for next week and ship the runbook.

Best,

Alex — thanks for the context and the incumbent numbers, that helps. Below is the technical probe plan we recommend and what we'll capture during the PoC. I've attached a compact runbook (poc-runbook.md) and a detailed traffic CSV for your load generator.

Probe plan (summary)
- Window: Two parts: (A) synthetic replay (48 hours, 3x baseline traffic bursts to profile tail behavior) and (B) 2-hour live canary (5% production-like traffic) for side-by-side comparison.
- Traffic shapes: follow attached CSV; includes token-length buckets (short: <40 tokens, medium: 40-120, long: >120). We recommend running medium-heavy for the replay to stress tail.
- Concurrency: target steady concurrency of 64 concurrent in-flight requests for sync calls during replay; for streaming, simulate 10 concurrent streams during steady and spikes to 40 concurrent streams during burst windows.
- Throughput: baseline 200 qps, peak bursts up to 1k qps for 60s windows.
- Warm/cold cache accounting: run a pre-warm phase (30 mins sessions) to populate KV/prefix caches. Then a cold-start sweep where we flush caches and replay a subset of traffic to capture cold-start characteristics. Acceptance gating will require passing the warm-cache run and recording cold-start delta separately (we'll report both).

Metrics we will collect (hosted):
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 latencies (request ingress -> response delivered to client).
- Token-level breakdown (model decode time vs network vs pre/post-processing).
- GPU utilization, per-GPU latency percentiles, and model fallback counts (we can expose these as part of the hosted debug bundle during the PoC).
- Error rates and retries, and streaming connect/drop events.

Acceptance criteria suggestion (example)
- Warm-cache: p95 <= 140ms, p99 <= 360ms (side-by-side with incumbent; Redwood must be demonstrably within or better than incumbent to pass).
- Cold-start: p95 <= incumbent_p95 + 40ms (we will report deltas).

Operational notes
- We'll run the hosted endpoints in the us-west region to minimize added network hops.
- Data: use redwood-sample-scrubbed dataset (no PHI) — provide your mapping file for any edge-case tokens you want excluded.
- Security — Ben will coordinate the SOC2 artifacts with your procurement contact.

Deliverables before kickoff
- Redwood: PoC runbook (attached), traffic_profile.csv, access token/endpoint, instrumentation checklist.
- Orpheus: confirmation of streaming ratio, procurement contact, list of pre-approved sample queries for the replay.

Happy to run through this in a 30-min call; I can present the run order and the monitoring dashboard.

Ben Carter
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference
